clue.text: Warning against excessive spit and polish in the field?

definitions.text: Warning against excessive spit and polish in the field?

parts.words: Warning against excessive spit and polish
parts.note: surface reading: a caution to soldiers against too much fussy cleaning of boots and kit
setter's reading: a sign on a farm gate warning walkers about the animal grazing there, with spit and polish standing for its slang name

explanation.walkthrough: Spit and polish is military fussiness about shining kit, which British soldiers call bull, short for bullshit; 'in the field' turns it into a farmer's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the familiar notice posted on gates where a dangerous animal is kept, and here it doubles as advice to avoid pointless military smartness.

clue.text: Choice oriental reading

parts.note: E stands for eastern, and oriental means eastern
a lection is a reading from scripture in a church service

explanation.surface: A selection of Eastern literature is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: A lection is a passage read aloud in church, the word behind lectern.
explanation.definitionFit: An election is the act of choosing, as in by vote, so it is a synonym for choice.

clue.text: Pole responsible for a long poem?

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article before a vowel
an ode is an elaborate lyric poem, often of some length

explanation.surface: A person from Poland is credited with writing an epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish writer, but it is the electrical sense; the question mark admits that an ode is not always long.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode of a battery or cell, one of its two poles.

clue.text: Laid off politician given to procrastination

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters before it are spoiled into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A sacked politician turns out to be a habitual time-waster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid off' reads as made redundant; only 'off' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory describes someone slow to act who keeps delaying, which is a person prone to putting things off.

clue.text: Head-ache for girl on border

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, so the girl's name sits on top of the border

parts.note: Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A girl standing at a frontier is causing someone trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Megrim is an old word for migraine, a severe one-sided pain in the head.

clue.text: Find fault with vestibule woodwork

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
an entry is an entrance hall or vestibule

explanation.surface: Someone criticises the joinery in a house's front hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the craft of making things from timber, and also the timber work produced, so woodwork.

clue.text: Something worn in the dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short open jacket ending above the waist
second meaning: a Spanish dance in triple time

explanation.surface: A dancer wears a costume during the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short Spanish-style jacket and a lively Spanish dance, the one Ravel wrote famous music for.

clue.text: Weather-front may turn out very much to my liking

indicators.note: turning out means proving different from expected, so the letters come out in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen
taken as written, doing double duty with the signal

explanation.surface: A forecaster hopes the coming cold front will bring the weather they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is part of the fodder as well as of the signal 'may turn out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something after your own heart is exactly the kind you like, an idiom for being much to your taste.

clue.text: Plant in a gentle manner

indicators.note: a manner is a way of doing something, hinting that the preceding words are to be done in a new way, rearranged

parts.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to set a seedling into the ground softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a gentle manner' reads as one adverbial phrase, but only 'manner' works as the signal; the other three words are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild rose bush, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Withdrawn from a jester's back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back here means backwards, so the jester's name is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a fool is a court jester

explanation.surface: Something has been pulled away from behind a court clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jester's back' looks like the jester's body, but it means the jester word turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof keeps their distance and stays reserved, which is what withdrawn describes in a person.

clue.text: Help one to come back after car-crash in Southern Greece

indicators.note: after places the returned help-one words behind the crashed car in the answer
coming back means returning the way it went, so these words are read right to left
a crash leaves a vehicle mangled, so the letters of the car are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to aid is to help
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone helps an accident victim recover after a car crash on holiday in the Peloponnese.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a news story, but the order is the wrecked car first, then help-one turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a region in the central Peloponnese peninsula, the southern part of mainland Greece.

clue.text: Permitted peer to stagger out full

indicators.note: staggering is lurching about unsteadily, so these letters lurch out of their order

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lord is allowed to totter out of a banquet after eating too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in a synonym as well as a word taken as written, so the solver has to find the short word for permitted first.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, especially well fed after a meal, a formal synonym for full.

clue.text: Bad to be charged with energy in reverse

indicators.note: going in reverse means travelling backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a live wire is one charged with electrical energy

explanation.surface: Something wicked is generated when electricity runs the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is a strong word for wicked or morally wrong, so it serves as a synonym for bad.

clue.text: Usual term for rude class

parts.note: common in the old sense of coarse or vulgar
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Someone asks what people normally call an ill-mannered group of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is the British word for a class or year group at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Common form is the standard, routine wording of a document or phrase, the customary expression for something.

clue.text: Friends upset by jam in knockabout farce

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so the word for friends is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pals are friends
to jam is to stick fast

explanation.surface: Mates get annoyed when a pot of preserve is thrown in a comic routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' suggests the fruit spread of custard-pie comedy, but it is the verb meaning to wedge.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy full of falls and blows, the style of a knockabout farce.

clue.text: Eventually get something fishy on a close associate

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the fishy part is followed by the associate

parts.note: a fin is something belonging to a fish
an ally is a close associate or partner

explanation.surface: In time you discover your best friend is up to something suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' suggests a suspicious act, but it is literal: a part of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Finally means at last, after a long time or a delay, which is the sense of eventually.

clue.text: Storm that ruined a party?

parts.note: torn means ripped, damaged or ruined
taken as written
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A bad storm spoiled an outdoor celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: A do is everyday British slang for a party or social event.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, so it is a kind of storm.

clue.text: He makes' cuts in plate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who digs ditches, cutting into the ground
second meaning: a wooden platter for serving or carving food

explanation.surface: An engraver cuts lines into a metal printing plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe is the scan's; the first half is a ditch digger, and 'cuts in plate' falsely suggests engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher is a digger of trenches and also an old wooden board or platter on which food was served.

clue.text: Worker taken in by girl in Spanish port

indicators.note: being taken in means being received inside, so the worker goes within the girl's name

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
the worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer is charmed by a young woman in a Mediterranean harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a city and seaport on the Costa Blanca of south-eastern Spain.

clue.text: Director getting drink for janitor

parts.note: Sir Peter Hall, the English theatre director who founded the Royal Shakespeare Company
porter is a dark beer, a type of stout

explanation.surface: A boss fetches a beverage for the building's caretaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' looks like any manager, but it names one particular theatre director, Peter Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall porter looks after the entrance and building of a hotel or block, the job of a doorkeeper or caretaker.

clue.text: Ventilator in gallery\

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slatted opening that lets air through while keeping rain out
second meaning: the great art museum in Paris

explanation.surface: An air vent is fitted inside an art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a set of angled slats for ventilation and the famous Paris art museum.

clue.text: Most unusual to see a king in repose

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the article and royal letter go within the word for repose

parts.note: rest is repose
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: It is a rare sight indeed to catch a monarch sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, meaning least common, so most unusual.

clue.text: Look average it is said

indicators.note: it is said means spoken out loud, so the word wanted only sounds like the synonym for average

parts.note: the mean is the average of a set of numbers

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at what is ordinary, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A mien is a person's appearance or bearing, especially the expression on their face, which is their look.

clue.text: Love to scold or deliver a harangue

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like the letter O
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold angrily

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between tenderness and a telling-off ends up giving a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a long pompous speech, which is what delivering a harangue amounts to.

clue.text: Trouble over a sieve

indicators.note: over as in turned over, knocked about so these letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a kitchen strainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare word: boult is an old spelling of bolt, to sift flour, so a boulter is a sifting sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulter, more often spelt bolter, is a sieve or cloth for sifting meal from bran.

clue.text: "Corpse in the Vehicle" lawsuit

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a case is a lawsuit heard in court

explanation.surface: The title of a crime story about a body found in a car, which is also the name of a legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a book title; ignore them and read 'Corpse' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Carcase is an older spelling of carcass, a dead body, especially of an animal, so a corpse.

clue.text: Poetic effusion that might make some family rich

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A gushing poem could earn a fortune for a few relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling, the kind of outpouring an effusion suggests.

clue.text: Step actor takes to be come a witness

indicators.note: becoming something is turning into it, so these letters are changed into a fresh order

parts.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer steps down from the stage to give evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'be come'; read it as become, the change signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker who watches an event, which is one meaning of a witness.
